title: How do we choose the scale for the runs in eight matches?
description: The runs scored by a cricketer in eight matches go from zero to one hundred. A scale of one unit for ten runs keeps the graph short, and Keeko's doubt, that one unit for one run is more exact, is checked against how tall the bars would grow.
teaching_notes: One idea: pick a scale that fits the largest number on the page, then divide every number by it. Watch for students who keep one unit for one run and run out of paper.

source: The number of runs scored by Smriti in each of the 8 matches: Match 1 80, Match 2 50, Match 3 10, Match 4 100, Match 5 90, Match 6 0, Match 7 90, Match 8 50. Draw a bar graph.
video_script.why: The child learns to choose a scale that fits the largest number, and to divide each number by the scale to get the height of its bar.
video_script.substitution: Find the smallest and largest numbers, choose one unit for ten runs, and divide every score by ten.
video_script.anchor: the table of runs scored by the cricketer in each of the eight matches
video_script.wrong_answer: one unit should be one run, because that is more exact
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko keeps one unit for one run. The tallest bar would then be one hundred units, too tall for the page.
video_script.payoff_line: The bars are eight, five, one, ten, nine, zero, nine and five units tall

final_answer.value: scale 1 unit = 10 runs; bars of 8, 5, 1, 10, 9, 0, 9 and 5 units
final_answer.spoken: one unit stands for ten runs, and the bars are eight, five, one, ten, nine, zero, nine and five units tall

hold_back: scale 1 unit = 10 runs; bars of 8, 5, 1, 10, 9, 0, 9 and 5 units
maths_rules: with 1 unit = 1 run the tallest bar would be 100 units
video_script.design: One idea: choose a scale so the largest number fits, then divide each number by it. The table stays on the board all video and the heights are written beside it.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; the table of runs in matches 1 to 8: 80, 50, 10, 100, 90, 0, 90, 50, with a cricket bat and ball

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.table: the table of runs in the eight matches appears with a cricket bat and ball
marks.ask: an empty pair of lines appears with a question mark over the vertical line

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This idea is from your book, and it is about cricket.
<bookmark mark='table'/>A young cricketer scored runs in eight matches. Some counts are small, and one is a hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How tall should the bars be for such different scores?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board and Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a page with a bar of 100 small squares running off the top and a second bar of 10 squares fitting the page; the words fit the page appear

marks.long: a bar of one hundred small squares runs off the top of the page
marks.short: a bar of ten squares fits well on the page
marks.fit: the words fit the page appear

narration: <bookmark mark='long'/>If the biggest bar is a hundred squares tall, it runs off the page.
<bookmark mark='short'/>If one square stands for many runs, the bar is short enough to fit.
<bookmark mark='fit'/>We choose how much one unit stands for. This choice is called the scale.

marks.first: 80, 50, 10 and 100 are written for the first four matches
marks.last: 90, 0, 90 and 50 are written for the last four matches

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Given, the first four matches had eighty, fifty, ten and one hundred runs.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last four had ninety, zero, ninety and fifty runs.

beats.on_screen: To find: a scale, and the bar graph of the runs

marks.find: the words a scale and the bar graph of the runs are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to choose the scale and find the height of every bar.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the smallest score is 0 and the largest is 100
narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step one, find the smallest and the largest number. The smallest is zero.
<bookmark mark='large'/>The largest is one hundred, so the tallest bar must stand for one hundred.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: one unit for one run needs 100 units, which is too tedious; take the scale 1 unit length = 10 runs

marks.tedious: the words 1 unit = 1 run are crossed out, with 100 units written beside them
marks.ten: the scale 1 unit length = 10 runs is written

narration: <bookmark mark='tedious'/>Step two, choose the scale. One unit for one run needs a hundred units, which is far too long to draw.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Let one unit stand for ten runs. The tallest bar then needs only ten units.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Step three, divide each count of runs by ten to get the height of its bar. Eighty divided by ten is eight.
<bookmark mark='five'/>Fifty divided by ten is five.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Ten divided by ten is one.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>One hundred divided by ten is ten.

marks.zero: 0 / 10 = 0 is written for match 6 and the bar has no height
marks.rest: 90 / 10 = 9 and 50 / 10 = 5 are written for matches 7 and 8

narration: <bookmark mark='nine'/>Step four, finish the rest. Ninety divided by ten is nine.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>Zero divided by ten is zero, so in match six there is no bar to raise.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>Ninety gives nine again, and fifty gives five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: scale 1 unit = 10 runs; bars of 8, 5, 1, 10, 9, 0, 9 and 5 units

marks.pay: the answer line is boxed and the eight heights are written under the eight matches

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The bars are eight, five, one, ten, nine, zero, nine and five units tall.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the bar graph
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble says one unit should be one run; the bubble is struck through; a tall bar of 100 units runs off the top of the page; the scale 1 unit = 10 runs is shown beside a bar of 10 units

marks.tall: a bar of one hundred units runs off the top of the page
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and a bar of 10 units fits the page

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one unit should be one run, because that is more exact.
<bookmark mark='tall'/>But then the bar for one hundred runs would be one hundred units tall. It would run off the page.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>With one unit for ten runs, every bar still shows its runs, and the whole graph fits.
